[EFFECT] The day of the week has a **non-monotonic, categorical** effect on predicted demand — it does not simply rise or fall as the day number increases. Saturday (day 6) and Sunday (day 0) both show the widest spread of SHAP contributions: they can reach the highest positive boosts (around +0.55 in log scale) at certain hours, but also produce the deepest negative penalties (around −0.85 to −0.90) at others. Midweek days (Monday through Thursday) display narrower, more moderate contributions, while Friday leans slightly positive overall. This wide spread on weekends reflects the fact that demand patterns within those days vary dramatically by hour — leisure peaks and quiet overnight hours pull in opposite directions.

[IMPORTANCE] With a global importance score of 0.173 and a **rank of 4 out of 9**, weekday is a meaningful but secondary driver of demand. It is considerably less influential than the hour of day (rank 1, importance 0.83) and slightly below year and temperature (both around 0.20), but it clearly outweighs humidity, weather situation, wind speed, and holiday.

[RECOMMENDATION] Because the effect of weekday is especially large and variable on weekends — with both big demand surges and deep quiet periods depending on the hour — staffing and bike rebalancing plans should treat Saturday and Sunday as distinct operational profiles rather than scaling from weekday baselines, ensuring extra capacity is available during weekend peak hours while avoiding over-provisioning overnight.
